problem: Find the equation of the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=2({e}^{2x})-5.$

feedback.problem: Suppose that $f(x)=2({3}^{x-5})-3.$ Given that $f(x)\to a$ as $x\to -\infty ,$ then $a=$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's plot the graph of $y=f(x):$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943819/assets/3e2c3036fb3f8c92ab09067fca4117e6fead9026e2fd926e174fefbe9037cbcf.png)

Since the function approaches the line $y=-3$ as $x\to -\infty ,$ we conclude that

$$
f(x)\to -3\,\text{as}\,x\to -\infty .
$$

Therefore, $a=-3.$
